articles.title: Real Madrid star Raul Asencio in trouble again! Banned from driving for 8 months days before trial over alleged sharing of explicit video involving minor
articles.summary: Football News: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio has been banned from driving for 8 months after a drink-driving conviction, just days before a trial concerning alleged distribution of explicit video involving a minor.
articles.body: Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio has been handed an eight-month driving ban and a fine of around £12,350 (approx. $16,685) after being convicted of drink-driving in Spain. The 23-year-old was stopped in the early hours while driving a Porsche Macan GTS in Gran Canaria and recorded a breathalyser reading almost four times above the country's legal limit. The conviction comes just days before Asencio is due in court over a separate case involving the alleged sharing and distribution of intimate footage involving a minor, for which he has previously denied the allegations. Real Madrid have also opened disciplinary proceedings against their academy graduate following the latest incident.Asencio stopped at 6.30am in Gran CanariaAsencio was stopped by police at a breathalyser checkpoint in San Bartolome de Tirajana, in the south of Gran Canaria, at around 6.30am on August 16.The Real Madrid defender had been driving a Porsche Macan GTS when officers stopped him and carried out a breath test. According to the Daily Mail, his reading came back at 0.90 milligrams of alcohol per litre of exhaled breath, while Spain's legal drink-drive limit is 0.25 milligrams per litre.He subsequently pleaded guilty to drink-driving at a fast-track hearing three days later.The conviction, which emerged on Wednesday, resulted in an eight-month suspension of his driving licence and a financial penalty of €14,400, equivalent to around $16,685. The fine was set at €120 (approx. $139) per day over four months.The incident has now also triggered action from Real Madrid. According to journalist Melchor Ruiz, the club has opened an extraordinary disciplinary file against Asencio, meaning his conduct will now be assessed internally as well as having already resulted in a criminal conviction.Under the collective agreement between La Liga and the AFE (Association of Spanish Footballers), the incident could potentially be treated as either a serious or very serious disciplinary offence.If Real Madrid classifies it as a serious offence, Asencio could face a suspension from his salary lasting between two and 10 days. A very serious classification would carry a substantially heavier punishment, with a salary suspension of between 11 and 30 days, while a fine could reach 25 per cent of the first €100,000 of his monthly salaryA difficult period for the Real Madrid defenderThe timing of the drink-driving conviction is particularly significant because Asencio is already dealing with a separate legal case that is due to reach trial on Thursday.The Real Madrid defender is facing proceedings over the alleged sharing and distribution of an intimate video involving a minor, as well as allegations that the footage was distributed without consent.Both alleged victims have since withdrawn their complaints against Asencio, which has opened the possibility of him being acquitted.However, public prosecutors are still seeking a two-and-a-half-year prison sentence if he is convicted. Prosecutors have also indicated that they will withdraw the charges against Asencio if the alleged victims confirm in court the apologies they say he offered them during the judicial investigation.Asencio has previously denied the allegations. In May 2025, he released a statement in which he fiercely rejected the accusations made against him.The separate case dates back to an incident at a beach club in Gran Canaria on June 15, 2023..What happened in the separate video case?Asencio's former Real Madrid academy teammates Ferran Ruiz, Juan Rodriguez and Andres Garcia are also due to stand trial in connection with the 2023 incident.Ruiz, Rodriguez and Garcia were arrested in September 2023 after allegations surrounding sexual activity involving two women at the beach club. The three former Real Madrid academy players are accused of having consensual sexual relations with the two women but allegedly recording and distributing sexual videos without their consent.Asencio is not accused of being involved in that alleged incident itself.He was initially interviewed by police in connection with the investigation before subsequently becoming part of the wider case over the alleged sharing of the footage.Real Madrid's patience with Asencio is being testedThe legal issues come during a period in which Asencio's position at Real Madrid has already become considerably less secure than it once appeared.The defender was previously viewed as one of the leading products of the club's academy after breaking into the first team, but his standing has declined in recent months. He is currently out injured and, according to the report, has fallen down the pecking order to the point where he is not even considered the club's fourth-choice central defender.His relationship with the club has also reportedly been complicated by his decision to remain at Real Madrid during the summer transfer window, despite the club's preference for him to leave. That decision was reported to have prevented the hierarchy from pursuing further defensive reinforcements.The drink-driving conviction now adds another issue for the club to consider, with Real Madrid's extraordinary disciplinary proceedings potentially bringing an internal punishment on top of the legal consequences already imposed by the Spanish court.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fifa abre inscrições para voluntários na Copa do Mundo Feminina 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, serão 32 seleções e 64 partidas, incluindo a final, no dia 25 de julho, no Maracanã.
articles.summary: Ao todo, serão 32 seleções e 64 partidas, incluindo a final, no dia 25 de julho, no Maracanã.
articles.body:
A Fifa abriu nesta quinta-feira (3) as inscrições para voluntários na Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027, no Brasil.

Muitas memórias têm forma. Mascotes, credenciais, lembranças do trabalho dessas voluntárias em megaeventos esportivos.

"Eu gostava muito de ajudar as pessoas. Tipo: estou perdida! Vamos embora que eu ajudo”, diz a enfermeira Lívia Beatriz de Almeida.

Repórter: E dá para ver os jogos? Lívia Beatriz de Almeida: Dá, dá.

Fifa abre inscrições para voluntários na Copa do Mundo Feminina 2027 — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O prazer de servir e trocar experiências move milhares de pessoas em uma Copa do Mundo. Em 2014, foi assim com a Lívia, no Rio de Janeiro. Já a Renata José Ferreira de Lima aproveitou os jogos daquele mundial para testar os conhecimentos de inglês.

"Ter essa experiência no meu currículo, porque era uma oportunidade de ouvir a língua inglesa e também de participar de um evento mundial”, conta a secretária executiva Renata José Ferreira de Lima.

A professora Paula Rodrigues Pontes mora em Atlanta, nos Estados Unidos, onde trabalhou na Copa do Mundo masculina de 2026 como supervisora de outros voluntários.

"Atlanta foi uma sede maravilhosa. A Fifa Fan Fest foi um sucesso, mais do que o esperado. Tudo ficava mais ou menos concentrado naquela região. A diferença que a gente vê no Brasil é... Falou que é futebol, a gente vai ver festa para todo lado” diz a professora Paula Rodrigues Pontes.

A inscrição oficial de interessados no site da Fifa começou nesta quinta-feira (3). Elas e eles vão passar por um processo seletivo para preencher cerca de 6 mil vagas para voluntários nas oito cidades-sedes do mundial.

"A minha família é de Belo Horizonte, sou de BH. Vamos fazer essa coisa mineira de fazer todo mundo se apaixonar por pão de queijo. Mas, se você escolhe ir para outro lugar, é com você. Viajar, estadia etc”, explica Paula Rodrigues Pontes.

Ao todo, serão 32 seleções e 64 partidas, incluindo a final, no dia 25 de julho, no Maracanã, com a taça da Copa Feminina em jogo. Entre os voluntários, a disputa é pelo troféu da melhor hospitalidade.

"Principalmente quando a sede é no Rio de Janeiro. A gente sempre puxa a sardinha para o nosso lado”, brinca Lívia Beatriz de Almeida.

articles.title: La caída del Pitbull del gol que malvive en las calles adicto al crack: "Es mejor si creen que estoy muerto"
articles.standfirst: La adicción al crack lleva al exfutbolista Régis Pitbull a vivir en la calle: "No quiero que nadie sepa que existo"
articles.summary: La adicción al crack lleva al exfutbolista Régis Pitbull a vivir en la calle: "No quiero que nadie sepa que existo"
articles.body: Régis Pitbull, futbolista brasileño que llegó a jugar en Ponte Preta, Corinthians y Vasco, malvive en las calles de Sao Paulo víctima de su adicción al crack. "Es mejor si creen que estoy muerto... No quiero que nadie sepa que existo", declaró el exfutbolista de 49 años a Emilio Botta en 'Globo Esporte'. Coritiba, Kyoto Sanga (Japão), Gaziantepspor (Turquia), Daejon Citzen (Coreia do Sul), Corinthians, Vasco, Bahia, Portuguesa, Inter de Limeira, ABC, Al Nasr, Rio Branco-MG, Poços de Caldas-MG y Sao Raimundo-AM, sumó 49 goles en 170 partidos a lo largo de su carrera. Régis Pitbull, irreconocible tras años de adicción a la cocaína en polvo procesada con bicarbonato de sodio y agua, ha tenido problemas con la justicia y ya fue detenido por agredir al administrador de su edificio. El exfutbolista, que no oculta su adicción, convive con la dependencia química desde sus inicios en el fútbol. En dos ocasiones dio positivo en controles antidopaje por consumo de marihuana. Fue suspendido, volvió a jugar y siguió adelante con su vida antes de verse consumido por sustancias más fuertes que le arrebataron el control de su propia existencia.

articles.title: Louisiana Judge Rules Against NCAA, Clearing Path for Ex-NFL Players to Join LSU Roster
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Lane Kiffin's chances of fielding former NFL players improved Thursday night when a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in a high-profile eligibility case.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Lane Kiffin's chances of fielding former NFL players improved Thursday night when a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in a high-profile eligibility case.

East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued his ruling the night before LSU was due to submit its 105-man roster to the Southeastern Conference, which last week announced heavy potential punishment for football and basketball teams that bring in ex-pros.

The ruling clears the way for LSU to list some former NFL players on its roster. How many games they might be eligible to play remains to be seen as the matter continues working its way through the courts.

"It's not about coach Kiffin. It's not about LSU. It's about treating these kids fairly," said Tony Clayton, an attorney for the athletes. "Today, justice was served. And justice was serve to the SEC. It was served like a cold cup of gumbo. And that judge forced him to eat it."

Jorden said he considered sanctions against the SEC and the NCAA but ruled he was not ready to issue any at this time.

Jorden's decision followed a nearly nine-hour hearing in a courtroom near the LSU campus during which athlete after athlete took the stand to explain why they should be allowed to return to play college sports after turning pro. The commissioner of the powerful SEC argued against them, and the league doubled down by filing a lawsuit against the school in federal court. That lawsuit could now become the SEC's best chance at preventing former pros from playing this season.

The hearing was attended by Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill, who filed a brief in the case on behalf of the athletes. While she did not make any arguments in court, she spoke after the ruling and referred to the SEC's federal lawsuit against LSU as "legal garbage."

"It was an attempt at a collateral attack on this judge that it was a message to say that, 'If you rule against us here, that we're going to try and go to federal court in Alabama and get a ruling that is a federal ruling that binds you,'" Murrill said. "I don't think this judge was impressed by that threat."

The courtroom confrontation came just two days before 11th-ranked LSU opens the season at home against Clemson. Jorden scheduled the hearing over his temporary injunction preventing the NCAA from barring former pros or fifth-year college athletes, a stance reiterated by the SEC and other Power Four conferences in potential punishments adopted last week.

Former NFL players testify about modest pay in pros

Former New Orleans Saints defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright, two players who now expect to suit up for LSU within weeks, sat next to each other in the gallery as the hearing began and both took the stand to say they would have not tried to turn pro had they known they might get another year in college.

Harris and Wright said they each earned about $1 million in college. Harris said he was paid just $190 in travel expenses by the Saints and spent all of his time with the club rehabbing a foot injury. Wright said he was paid a $25,000 signing bonus by Philadelphia before his brief time with the Browns and would gladly pay that back for the chance to play for LSU.

While both former Mississippi players were unsure how soon they might make their LSU debut, they said after the hearing that they expect to play when the Tigers visit Ole Miss on Sept. 19.

Two LSU soccer players, Jazmin Ferguson and Jocelyn Ollivierre, won earlier court orders and have already played this season. Ferguson testified that she was paid $4,500 by a USL team, but ended her contract and paid the money back in hopes of clearing the way to play for the Tigers again. Two LSU softball players also testified.

The athletes testified after SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey was on the stand for more than two hours, defending the league's authority to enforce its longstanding rules barring former pros from returning to play at its 16 member schools, and enforce newly outlined fines and suspensions against programs and coaches. He said school presidents and chancellors felt that they needed to establish a line between professional and college sports and that there needed to be ways to hold schools accountable.

"The line between professional sports and college sports needs to be maintained," Sankey testified, adding that the league was concerned about incoming athletes being displaced from limited roster spots.

As he spoke, the SEC filed the federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU and its leadership, alleging the school had "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes" in defiance of league rules. The court filing against one of the league's founding members in 1933 seeks an injunction barring LSU from violating the SEC's First Amendment rights by forcing it to "associate with conduct that is contrary to the conference's purpose and mission."

Legal experts said the filing was a backup in case the SEC lost in state court. Outside the courthouse in Baton Rouge, Clayton said: "I got a problem with that. I mean, you go around, you can file this suit in any state. You're suing LSU. Sue them in Louisiana. You go to our nemesis: Alabama. Really? So, that lets you know what the commissioner is all about."

In questioning Sankey, attorneys for the athletes cited numerous examples of when SEC eligibility rules align with NCAA rules, suggesting the potential of collusion. They questioned why league members met last week to adopt stiff penalties for the very actions addressed in the Louisiana state court's temporary injunction against the NCAA.

The attorneys also asked why the SEC singled out players who signed contracts with specific U.S.-based leagues — the NFL, NBA and WNBA — but not overseas pro leagues or women's pro soccer leagues. When Sankey tried to qualify an answer about whether the SEC had previously punished a school for adding a player with previous pro experience, Clayton said, "I didn't ask how to build a clock. I'm just asking what time it is."

Sankey acknowledged that there had previously been no such punishment, but that it had been considered against Alabama last basketball season when the Crimson Tide briefly added a former G League player.

Players going to court has become common

The players in question also include former Denver Broncos defensive back Blake Cotton, who like Harris and Wright is hoping to join LSU and Kiffin .

Wright, who played for Kiffin last season at Ole Miss, started practicing at LSU this week, too late to be eligible for Saturday's home opener against Clemson under the NCAA's required seven days of practice. Harris has committed to LSU, while Cotton, who played at Utah last fall, has been recruited by Kiffin.

All three are among a host of athletes who've argued in lawsuits around the country that they are unfairly being denied an opportunity to spend a fifth year in college under newly adopted NCAA rules allowing for five full years of competition. In all, the NCAA says there are approximately 450 athlete plaintiffs seeking additional eligibility through litigation, with some 300 of them winning the ability to play at least for now.

NCAA attorney Taylor Askew said the number of disputes actually strengthens the argument that the NCAA is trying to enforce rules fairly.

"Was it applied inconsistently? Absolutely not," Askew said. "That can't be arbitrary. It's consistency."

The athletes in the case who signed pro contracts have argued they did so only because current rules that would have allowed them another college season weren't adopted until after their decisions to leave for the chance to make an NFL roster.

The SEC contends the question before the judge should be a narrow one regarding whether the conference "can enforce and require its member institutions to comply with SEC rules." The SEC's proposed punishments include significant fines, up to half-season suspensions for coaches and member universities' loss of voting privileges on league business matters.

Sankey provided an affidavit stating that SEC university presidents had voted 15-0 in favor of the new rules, with LSU's Wade Rousse abstaining.

The fight over eligibility between schools and their own conferences and the NCAA has simmered for months and spilled into politics.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry posted on X to attorneys general in Georgia and South Carolina that "calling them 'NFL players' is at best disingenuous, and at worst intentionally deceptive."

"They are not professional football players circling back after years in the NFL," Landry wrote. "They are college players who were told, by the NCAA, that they were done. So they took the only door that was open — only to watch the NCAA change the lock behind them."

articles.title: After winless 2025, UMass beats power conference foe for the first time as a 29.5-point underdog against Rutgers
articles.summary: Before Thursday night, the Minutemen's last win came in October of 2024.
articles.body:
UMass finally has a win over a power conference program. And it wasn't even close, either.

The Minutemen upset Rutgers 37-21 as 29.5-point underdogs on Thursday to begin the 2026 college football season. Since moving up to college football's top level in 2012, UMass had never beaten a team in one of the power conferences before it pulled off what will assuredly be one of the biggest upsets of the season on the first night of play in Week 1.

Rutgers QB Dylan Lonergan committed four turnovers. His third interception with 4:35 to go ended any chance of a miracle comeback for the Scarlet Knights, who looked like the far inferior opponent to a team that hadn't won a game since Oct. 26, 2024.

UMass QB Pop Watson threw three touchdowns in the first half. The Virginia Tech transfer is a Massachusetts native and went back to his home state after three years with the Hokies and just one TD pass over 63 attempts.

The victory is also the first for UMass coach Joe Harasymiak. He was hired to succeed Don Brown after serving as Rutgers' defensive coordinator from 2022 through 2024. The Minutemen went 0-12 in Harasymiak's first season in 2025. That season included a one-point loss to FCS-level Bryant and just a singular one-score loss to an FBS opponent.

UMass has been one of the most hapless programs in college football since moving up to the FBS level. The 1998 FCS champions have never won more than four games in a season over the past 14 years, and that's only happened twice. UMass has won two or fewer games in eight of the 13 previous full seasons and went 0-4 in 2020.

Overall, the Minutemen were just 26-134 entering Thursday night's game.

Even if UMass gets to a bowl for the first time in program history in 2026, the loss could be a harbinger of a rough season to come for Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights went 5-7 in 2025 and have games against USC, Indiana, Michigan and Penn State in Big Ten play. A second straight season without a postseason appearance is suddenly looking very, very likely. And September just started.

articles.title: DeAndre Hopkins Makes Coaching Debut for Georgia Tech vs. Deion Sanders' Colorado in New Photo
articles.summary: DeAndre Hopkins, who starred as a wide receiver over his 13 NFL seasons (2013-2025), made his debut on Thursday as Georgia Tech's assistant wide receivers coach when the Yellow Jackets began their 2026 season with a home game against head coach Deion Sanders' Colorado Buffaloes.
articles.body:
DeAndre Hopkins, who starred as a wide receiver over his 13 NFL seasons (2013-2025), made his debut on Thursday as Georgia Tech's assistant wide receivers coach when the Yellow Jackets began their 2026 season with a home game against head coach Deion Sanders' Colorado Buffaloes.

Hopkins told his fans on Aug. 1 that he wasn't officially done with the NFL, but he made it clear he's chosen a coaching path at this time.

The 34-year-old played for the Houston Texans, Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans, Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens. He's a five-time All-Pro (three First Teams, two Second Teams) and five-time Pro Bowler who has amassed 1,006 catches, 13,295 receiving yards and 85 receiving touchdowns.

articles.title: 'They Out-Coached Me,' Rutgers HC Greg Schiano Reflects on Historic Loss to UMass
articles.summary: Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano took responsibility for the team's surprising 37-21 loss to UMass on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano took responsibility for the team's surprising 37-21 loss to UMass on Thursday night.

"I wanna congratulate UMass and coach Harasymiak, his staff and players," Schiano said after the game, per Sports Illustrated's Bryan Fischer . "They out coached us, they out-coached me, they out-played our players. We got licked tonight. There's no other thing to say about it."

UMass was able to emerge victorious despite entering the contest on a 16-game losing streak, which contained the team's 0-12 finish in 2025. The Minutemen also picked up their first win over a power conference opponent since 1978 (h/t CBS Sports' Austin Nivison ).

First look at Pro Bowler coaching for CFB team

USC HC Claps Back at Attendance Criticism

UMass received $1.55 million from the Scarlet Knights to play them on the road as well.

The Minutemen thrived on both sides of the ball during the first half, entering halftime with a 24-7 lead.

They extended their advantage to 30-7 before Rutgers could get on the board again, as a late comeback attempt by the Scarlet Knights fell short.

Schiano's team dealt with issues on both sides of the ball, as UMass finished with 397 yards of total offense. This included 200 rush yards.

Meanwhile, Rutgers only scored seven points through three quarters and committed four turnovers as a team.

The Scarlet Knights will attempt to bounce back in their next matchup, a clash with Boston College on Sept. 11.

articles.title: Brian Barry-Murphy: Head coach to become Cardiff's longest serving boss since Neil Warnock
articles.summary: Brian Barry-Murphy takes charge of his 63rd game for Cardiff City when they face Portsmouth on Saturday.
articles.body:
Brian Barry-Murphy will become Cardiff City's longest-serving boss since Neil Warnock on Saturday, 5 September.

The 48-year-old takes charge of his 63rd game as head coach when his side face Portsmouth at Fratton Park.

In doing so, he signifies the longest period of stability since Warnock departed the Welsh club seven years ago.

Barry-Murphy will surpass the total number of matches overseen by Neil Harris between November 2019 and January 2021.

It says a lot about Cardiff's recent managerial turbulence that the Irishman will claim this accolade after less than 450 days in charge.

He is the eighth permanent appointment - and the 10th when including caretaker bosses - to take charge at Cardiff since Warnock left in November 2019.

One person who will not get carried away by the accolade is Barry-Murphy himself. By his own admission, he is not one to reflect when there is work to be done.

"It's a great privilege to be at a club of this size and backed by so many incredible supporters. But I don't look back too often," the former Manchester City academy coach admitted when told about the milestone.

"I'm very focused on the now and trying to give the supporters more nights they can enjoy and less like [Wednesday's defeat to QPR]."

Cardiff can reach Championship play-offs - Bielik

Lawlor set to miss Wales' Nations League games

Barry-Murphy took the reins at Cardiff during a difficult period for the club after their first relegation to the third tier in 22 years.

The former Rochdale manager exceeded the average 277-day tenure of his predecessors by March of this year, when the Bluebirds were second in League One.

And like Warnock he delivered a promotion, although his came in the first season, to get Cardiff back into the Championship at the first attempt.

By winning 34 of his 62 games in charge of the Bluebirds thus far, Barry-Murphy has achieved that goal more often than not.

Average attendances for home games increased in League One - despite relegation the previous season - and will likely do so again this campaign.

The emergence of several talented youngsters and the style of play adopted during his spell has rejuvenated the feeling among Cardiff fans.

And after three draws and a defeat to start the campaign, the question now is whether he can maintain the positive feeling in the Championship.

Barry-Murphy is confident of it, even after a quiet transfer deadline day, during which Cardiff were unable to sign the targets their head coach wanted.

Many fans have voiced their concern about a lack of squad depth, with only four players recruited at the Cardiff City Stadium this summer.

But Barry-Murphy feels he has been backed in the transfer window and is pleased with the players at his disposal for a gruelling Championship season.

There would be no better way for the Irishman to mark his latest Bluebirds achievement than to claim his first Championship win on Saturday.

articles.title: Colorado takes down Georgia Tech on a blocked field goal as time expires
articles.summary: Boo Carter won the game for the Buffaloes.
articles.body:
Colorado's special teams unit redeemed itself on the last play of the game against Georgia Tech.

Boo Carter blocked Aidan Birr's game-winning field goal attempt as time expired to give the Buffaloes a 14-13 win over Georgia Tech .

Carter's block came after QB JuJu Lewis found Charlie Williams for a go-ahead TD with 37 seconds to go. Georgia Tech quickly got into field goal position after the TD, but Carter saved the day.

Before the block, Colorado's special teams shanked a punt, gave up a 100-yard kickoff return TD and had a game-tying field goal blocked in the fourth quarter itself. It had been a disastrous special teams showing for a Colorado team that looked a lot better up front than it did in 2025.

After averaging 3.5 yards a carry a season ago, Colorado's strength Thursday night was on the ground. Before that field goal block midway through the fourth quarter, Colorado ran the ball 15 straight times on a 17-play drive.

Lewis was 14-of-27 passing for 124 yards and a TD, but 60 of those yards came on the final drive. The Buffaloes rushed for 183 yards and converted over 40% of their third downs in offensive coordinator Brennan Marion's first game with the team.

Colorado rushed for more than 183 yards just once in 2025 when it ran 31 times for 193 yards against Wyoming.

It's a massive win for Deion Sanders after Georgia Tech beat the Buffaloes to open the 2025 season. Colorado went 3-9 in 2025 as it lost its final five games of the season. In that losing streak, Lewis sat out to end the season to preserve his redshirt freshman season.

That ultimately didn't matter as the NCAA implemented a five-seasons-in-five-years rule over the summer. But it was a clear sign that Colorado was committed to the former high-profile recruit as its starter of the future.

While the stats weren't especially pretty, the result was good. And so was the throw to Williams. It was Lewis' best throw of the night. If that's a sign of things to come for the Buffaloes, then Colorado should be a much better team than it was a season ago.

images.caption: Colorado is 1-0 after beating Georgia Tech. (Photo by Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) (Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

articles.title: Desvelan el motivo por el que una millonaria estrella del fútbol fue a entrenar en una furgoneta de 7.000 euros
articles.summary: Joao Neves, futbolista portugués del PSG con un salario anual de 9 millones de euros, sorprendió a todos al llegar al centro de entrenamiento del Paris Saint-Germain al volante de una modesta furgoneta de carga.
articles.body: Joao Neves, futbolista portugués del PSG con un salario anual de 9 millones de euros, sorprendió a todos al llegar al centro de entrenamiento del Paris Saint-Germain al volante de una modesta furgoneta de carga. La imagen se hizo viral y el diario luso 'Record' desvela el motivo por el que Joao Neves fue al entrenamiento en una furgoneta Peugeot Partner de 2021, valorada en 7.000 euros. El motivo por el que João Neves fue al entrenamiento del PSG en una furgoneta de carga: "Un seguidor (@Djaameel_) bien informado sobre lo que sucede en el PSG escribió en Twitter: "Para que conste, Jooo Neves llegó al Campus en una furgoneta, pero había una razón detrás de todo ello. Una razón que inspira aún más respeto y demuestra la clase de ser humano formidable que es. ¡El bicampeón de Europa llevaba en la parte trasera de su furgoneta cientos de artículos que donó a las obras benéficas de la Fundación PSG!"... Esto demuestra lo increíble y humilde que es, además de su espíritu de equipo".

articles.title: Stadium erupts into 'Messiii, Messiii' chant as match paused in Argentina to honour Lionel Messi - Watch
articles.summary: Football News: Argentina began paying tribute to Lionel Messi after the football great announced his retirement from international football earlier this week.The fir.
articles.body: Argentina began paying tribute to Lionel Messi after the football great announced his retirement from international football earlier this week.The first tribute came during the Copa Argentina match between Velez Sarsfield and Boca Juniors on Wednesday, when play was stopped in the 10th minute for a round of applause at the Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes.Fans across the stadium stood and applauded Messi, bringing the game to a halt for a brief moment.Two of Messi's former Argentina teammates, Leandro Paredes and Manuel Lanzini, were on the pitch during the tribute.The match later ended 0-0, with Boca Juniors winning the penalty shootout 4-3.The tribute follows a decision by the Argentine Football Association, which announced that referees will stop play in the 10th minute of every match in the upcoming round of the Clausura tournament, as well as in other men's and women's competitions across the country, to honour Messi's international career.Messi announced his international retirement after the 2026 FIFA World Cup, ending a career that lasted 21 years with the Argentina team.He finished with 125 goals and 68 assists in 207 appearances for Argentina.In his retirement message, Messi said the decision "hurts the depths of my soul", but added that he "knows the time has come" to stop representing his country.Messi's biggest achievement with Argentina came when he led the team to the 2022 FIFA World Cup title in Qatar. He also helped Argentina win the Copa America in 2021 and 2024, ending the country's 28-year wait for a major trophy.Although he is one of Argentina's biggest sporting icons, Messi has never played club football professionally in his home country. He moved to Barcelona at the age of 13 and built his career there.Messi has retired only from international football and continues to play club football for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The Women’s Super League’s official fantasy game is here. Can it be a success?
articles.summary: The new Women’s Super League season will be the first with an official fantasy game. Launched on August 19, 16 days before the start of the 2026-27 season, t...
articles.body:
The new Women's Super League season will be the first with an official fantasy game.

Launched on August 19, 16 days before the start of the 2026-27 season, the game is the next step in the league's pursuit of more engagement with existing fans and a broader toolkit to attract new ones.

The extremely popular Fantasy Premier League (FPL) game was born 24 years ago, ahead of the 2002-03 season. At the end of last season, FPL had over 13million users around the world.

Naturally, in the quickly evolving world of women's football, one can't just copy and paste what has achieved success in men's football when it comes to creating an addictive game where users create a team that earns points for WSL players' real-life performances.

"I think there was an assumption that core fans love playing fantasy," Joey Davidson, head of digital products at the WSL, tells The Athletic . "But I think we also had to acknowledge that a core fan of the Premier League, for example, was very different in their behaviours from a core fan from the WSL."

Prior to the launch of the official WSL Fantasy game, there was a very popular unofficial version. Aerial Fantasy by Even Sports launched properly in 2023 under the name "Fantasy WSL" and garnered over 80,000 users across three seasons before shuttering its WSL game at the end of last season. Even Sports still operates an NWSL equivalent.

"We genuinely love this game and this community," said Aerial Fantasy co-founder Dani Goncalves in a statement on their website. "However, after putting in all the time and effort to make it exist, we realised it also needed to sustain itself financially."

In the development of their own fantasy game, the WSL spoke to many creators of existing games out there, including FPL and Aerial. In the end, the WSL chose to work with Sportz Interactive, who handle UEFA's fantasy league offerings.

Davidson acknowledges the decision to partner with Sportz Interactive over Aerial has created some division amongst WSL fans.

"That's the main criticism we've had since launch," he said. "It obviously made it quite challenging for that portion of the audience to really buy into a WSL Football product."

Honor Wicks, co-host of women's football podcast Screamers, who had been playing Aerial Fantasy for the last two seasons, says that she will not be signing up to play WSL Fantasy despite previously talking about fantasy football on the podcast and having segments analysing picks in Aerial's game.

"I think this is probably because I was just feeling a bit disillusioned with not being able to continue with the Aerial fantasy game, which I really enjoyed," Wicks tells The Athletic . "

When it came to developing the official game, Davidson and his team came in with an open mind. They weren't exactly sure what a fantasy WSL game should look like when tailored specifically to WSL fans.

In December 2025, the WSL ran a research project to try to better understand the desires of their fanbase. Would they prefer a weekly match-prediction game or a trivia app over a traditional points-based, season-long team selection fantasy game?

"We explored everything and it wasn't just us presenting a lot of options," Davidson says. "We took it to fans and said: 'What do you actually want to play? What do you want to do week-to-week?' I think we engaged around 7,000 fans in the initial outreach."

The primary positive response was community. People play fantasy to connect with other fans and learn more about players and the league they love.

"Community is key to it all," Davidson said. "We needed a game which brought people closer to the league, close to what players exist, and needed it to be a mechanism for fans learning about what's going on in real life, which then brings you closer to other fans, letting fans find community."

El, an Arsenal fan based in London, says that playing fantasy has been a feature in her social circles built around football. She has signed up to play WSL Fantasy.

"I'm in leagues with some of the girls that I play football with as well, so we get a bit competitive with each other," El tells The Athletic . "Sometimes we'll chat about it at the pub after our training sessions; have a bit of banter about who's doing crap or who's doing well."

"I think creating leagues with other women's football fans from online communities is a really nice lead-up to the season starting," says Mia, a Manchester United fan based in Manchester, who has also signed up to play this year. "I'll be doing my research right up until the final day. It's fun to have something competitive and interactive to play."

In terms of deterrents to playing fantasy, one of the biggest issues the WSL identified was users creating a team at the beginning of the season, falling behind in the competition, and then dropping off entirely.

As a rapidly growing and adaptive league, Davidson and his team also wanted the game to remain open to new fans discovering the WSL throughout the year.

So how could a fan who doesn't discover the WSL until December or January not be made to wait until the next season begins in September to play the league's fantasy game?

The WSL's solution was the creation of the leg system. In addition to the traditional season-long classic league, every manager in WSL Fantasy will also compete in six mini-seasons, known as legs. Each one lasts between three and six matches. There will be prize-winners and leagues created for every leg.

"What we wanted to do is create that feeling: you're always there, you've always got a chance to win," says Davidson. "You've always got a chance to compete with your friends again. Whereas if it's just that season-long game, you kind of have got one opportunity a year, and that's the main thing we wanted to tackle."

Another bold choice the WSL made when developing their game was bundling selectable players from the WSL and the WSL2 together. The theory was that by increasing the number of players in the game, there would be more variable squad selections and outcomes. More players means less similar teams and, in turn, more strategy.

"You get to January, and in previous games, the game has really slowed down because everyone's got the same team. That's because the talent pool in what was a 12-club league was too small to support a game with real depth," Davidson says.

Other fantasy games have adopted this. Fantasy EFL, home to the official fantasy game of the second, third and fourth tiers of men's football, offers players 72 clubs to select from across three leagues.

These decisions, though, are certainly splitting opinion.

For Arsenal fan El, all the new rules felt a bit "confusing", and she wishes the format of WSL Fantasy WSL was "a bit simpler." Wicks agrees and feels that the WSL's new game is "convoluted".

While Mia believed that even as "intimidating" as it was to see all the WSL2 players included in the game, she saw their inclusion as a positive change, saying it would "encourage people to keep up with both leagues".

There is no concrete metric for success when it comes to WSL Fantasy. Davidson is not putting a ceiling on the league's targets or audience gains, partly because he believes this fantasy game can go beyond traditional core fans.

"We feel like we've designed a format here that has a much wider appeal because our game can appeal to people who are completely new to football," he says.

At the time of writing, Fantasy WSL has had over 25,000 sign-ups since its launch two weeks ago.

Around half the WSL's investment for this project is going into exclusive creator-, coach- and player-driven content surrounding Fantasy WSL. All this lives on the app itself as well as on YouTube and podcast streaming platforms. Cultural influence, conversation and engagement might be the real reward that the WSL is seeking to seize.

"In terms of what success looks like for everybody, it's more about reach," says Davidson. "It's not just a game. There's a whole content ecosystem which surrounds this."

articles.title: The Women’s Super League is back: What’s new, key match-ups and how to watch
articles.summary: If your crystal ball is looking a little murky, don’t worry, you’re not alone. With more teams, a broken title run and contrasting approaches to investment,...
articles.body:
If your crystal ball is looking a little murky, don't worry, you're not alone.

With more teams, a broken title run and contrasting approaches to investment, this could be the most uncertain season of the Women's Super League yet. We could even see its power dynamics majorly disrupted for the first time in years.

London City Lionesses finished sixth last season but have signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas, signalling a shift in the league's status quo. Manchester United are entering a new era, with former Hearts head coach Eva Olid replacing Marc Skinner, whose five-year tenure ended in August. Does their focus on youth mean a place in the top four is up for the taking? Who will be the kingmakers in a title race that feels more open now that Manchester City have ended Chelsea's run of six consecutive WSL titles? And who will emerge as the next England star as the women's game gears up for the 2027 World Cup?

Welcome to The Athletic 's mega preview of the new Women's Super League season.

Manchester City lifted the WSL trophy for the first time in a decade, ending a once-impenetrable Chelsea dynasty that had stretched for a record six seasons.

Who qualified for the Women's Champions League?

Champions City and runners-up Arsenal went straight into the league phase, while third-placed Chelsea earned a place in the final qualification round. They confirmed their place in the Champions League proper on Wednesday, beating Real Sociedad 6-2 on aggregate.

City's Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw finished top scorer for the third time in four seasons. The 29-year-old bagged 21 goals in 22 matches, becoming the first player to notch three 20-goal seasons. Those numbers are why City forked out the big bucks to keep hold of the Jamaica international for another four years. Can anyone beat her?

For fans in the United Kingdom, every game from the WSL and WSL2 will be shown on either Sky, the BBC or YouTube.

Opening the WSL season on Friday, London City vs Manchester United can be found on six Sky channels — including Sky Sports Main Event and Sky One. Chelsea vs Aston Villa on Saturday will be available on BBC One and BBC iPlayer. Brighton & Hove Albion's lunchtime clash with Arsenal will take the Sky's Main Event slot on Sunday, with the remaining games available on Sky Sports+, a streaming service included in Sky Q and Glass subscriptions and available on the Sky Sports app.

Sky Sports will remain the WSL's primary home, with 90 per cent of all matches (163 in total) to be shown live on Sky Sports, including the promotion play-off match at the end of the season. Some of those games will also be shown on the Sky Sports WSL YouTube channel. BBC will show the remaining 10 per cent of matches.

In May, the WSL announced it had reached a broadcast deal with CBS . For the United States audience, Paramount+ will stream 183 matches and CBS Sports Network will air one match per week, with select matches also airing on CBS Sports' Golazo Network.

First match : London City vs Manchester United, Friday, 7pm UK (3pm ET/12pm PT)

Manchester City vs Arsenal (October 4 and January 30): If Arsenal are to win a first title in eight seasons, this feels like their best chance. Last season's showdown between the eventual champions and the runners-up at the Joie Stadium didn't disappoint. Former City attacker Chloe Kelly arrived as a substitute and equalised for the team she forced a move to in the 83rd minute. Kelly kissed the Arsenal badge. Five minutes later, Iman Beney won it for City. City fans trolled Kelly. Kelly trolled back. It was glorious, delirious drama.

Tottenham Hotspur vs Manchester United (December 20 and February 7): A trio of ex-United coaching staff now at Tottenham taking on their former club. The battle for the last Champions League spot could be tighter than ever this year, and these fixtures may result in a changing of the guard.

Chelsea vs Arsenal (September 27 and March 28): The most historic rivalry in the WSL, now with added spice courtesy of Katie McCabe's switch to the blue side of London and Arsenal knocking their rivals out of Europe in last season's quarter-final. They faced off four times last year, with Arsenal's only defeat coming in the second leg of their Champions League clash, which Chelsea lost 3-2 on aggregate. Chelsea will be desperate to reclaim bragging rights.

Charlton Athletic vs Birmingham City (October 25 and January 10): In a roundabout way, Charlton have Birmingham to thank for one of the greatest days in their modern history. Charlton had been top of WSL2 going into the final day last season, but a 2-0 defeat against Birmingham meant they finished third. Birmingham won the title, runners-up Crystal Palace took the second automatic promotion spot, and Charlton were left to contend the inaugural WSL promotion-relegation play-off.

Facing Leicester City, who finished bottom of the top flight, Charlton goalkeeper Sophie Whitehouse saved four penalties in the shootout to send her side into the WSL for the first time. In October, Charlton and Birmingham will have a chance to reignite the rivalry.

Will this be the most competitive title race in recent years?

Yes. City, Arsenal and Chelsea, as always, are all title contenders, but it feels even tighter this season after City knocked Chelsea off their perch. The way they did so suggests they can do it again. However, as the cliche goes: getting to the top is hard, staying at the top is even harder. City approach this season with a different perspective, going from hunters to hunted. "We love that, we want that, we welcome that challenge," City midfielder Sam Coffey told The Athletic .

Like City last year, Arsenal are hungry after a seven-year title drought. They are talented enough to win the league but have been slow starters in recent years.

Change is afoot at Chelsea, but they will want to exact revenge. Manchester United have a new head coach and faced recruitment difficulties this summer, all the while watching the league's depth get stronger. It is not just the games between the top four that could be defining, with Tottenham, Brighton and London City licking their lips at the prospect of taking points off the biggest sides.

The relatively new kid on the block and an independent club disrupting the status quo went for high-profile names — Putellas, Mary Earps, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani — and got them.

Former Manchester United captain and London City player Katie Zelem, now at West Ham United, was not surprised by their signings. "Michelle Kang is a powerhouse," she told The Athletic . "Having been in it, you understand they won't stop until they get to the top."

Their strategy is to spend money on older stars first, in the hope that revenue will come later from a new fanbase and sponsorship deals . On the pitch, they want to qualify for the Champions League. It's ambitious.

Some argue they are destroying the game and the salary cap. An increase in spending creates a divide and wage inflation beyond a club's means. Financial regulations are in place to stop clubs from doing that, and there is no sense yet that London City have broken any financial rules.

Others argue a club investing and bringing such players into the league brings more eyeballs, which is beneficial for the game's growth.

London City may be less popular in the mid-table section where Brighton, Tottenham and Aston Villa are fighting to build their fanbases and compete. Whether this video-game-style assembly of individuals will gel remains to be seen.

How will the 2027 World Cup impact the season?

A year out from the biggest Women's World Cup in history (literally, in terms of teams but also magnitude and potential impact), players have an eye on Brazil. U.S. women's national team forward Alyssa Thompson, who joined Chelsea last summer, told The Athletic that her move to the WSL took into account the physical and tactical preparation it offered for next summer's action. "Playing in tournaments means you have to be playing every two days," the forward said.

"I always want to be prepared for the national team," said Switzerland midfielder Geraldine Reuteler when asked about her move to Arsenal this summer. "It's the right step for me to be here to improve my football skills."

England youth international Ruby Mace, who, despite being a No 6 most of her career, was deployed as a centre-back last season for Everton, is among the players having conversations with their teams about how they fit into squads. "My position was a big question mark," Mace said. "Playing in (midfield) this year hopefully can allow me the platform to showcase what I can do."

Players ensuring they're performing in the ideal positions for their national teams is paramount. Teams want to capitalise on marketing opportunities with potential World Cup stars, so it benefits all parties to strike a balance — or make a move to do so.

What can we expect from Manchester United's new era?

After a bittersweet season that saw United reach the quarter-finals of the Champions League for the first time, but fail to qualify for this season's edition, the club is entering a new era.

Skinner departed the club by mutual agreement after five seasons as head coach. In his place, Olid is taking on her first WSL role after guiding Hearts to their maiden Scottish league title.

A change of coach — bearing in mind that Olid will only be the third person to manage United since their reformation in 2018, following Casey Stoney and Skinner — is seismic in isolation, but it also comes with significant movement in the squad.

Six players have departed permanently, most notably Melvine Malard, who had the most goal involvements in the squad last season. The France forward joined Chelsea in a club-record sale. Full-back Andrea Medina and goalkeeper Janina Leitzig have been recruited. United also signed Hacken winger Monica Jusu Bah last week and Washington Spirit defender Rebeca Bernal before Thursday's transfer deadline.

Olid's appointment aligns with the club's desired direction, emphasising sustainable investment and bringing through young players from United's Carrington academy. As The Athletic reported , Skinner's doubts over United's approach to squad investment were a factor in his exit.

Teenagers Layla Drury (17), Jess Anderson and Scarlett Hill (both 18) signed professional contracts this summer and other youngsters who spent last year on loan are also expected to feature more heavily.

The shift to youth is a big change — United ranked at the bottom of the WSL for minutes given to under-21 players last season. Particularly on the men's side, the club has a rich history of bringing through Carrington graduates and relying on youth. Supporters are keen to see academy talents given a chance, but teams around them invested heavily. Given the physical and tactical challenges academy talents can face when stepping up to the WSL , can United's approach propel them back into the top three?

Which of the middle of the pack can actually have a go?

We say it every season. But for real this time, with gusto, the status quo might be in trouble! Or, you know, a little nervous. Sure, City, Arsenal and Chelsea will likely be the teams locked in a title race, but that fourth-place berth is not so straightforward, and we should not underestimate other teams' impact on the title race itself.

As discussed, London City have taken an ambitious approach. Beyond them, Spurs impressed under head coach Martin Ho in his first season, finishing fifth in the table. The club have backed him by signing defender Alice Sombath for a club-record fee (above £375,000), plus additions such as forward Kirsty Hanson and defender Caitlin Dijkstra. Last season's signings Signe Gaupset and Julie Blakstad should be more settled (and dangerous) in their second year. Victories against the established top three will be the aim.

It can sound wild that Liverpool – bottom of the WSL last winter break – are included here but summer recruitment has been strong (Vivien Endemann! Mao Itamura!) and the underlying attacking numbers last season were exceedingly positive. A teething year was always necessary given the style and managerial shift under Gareth Taylor. It won't be seamless but those at Liverpool believe they can start looking upwards.

Brighton were most people's picks for dark-horse hopefuls this season, particularly after reaching their first major final under former head coach Dario Vidosic in his second season in charge. But Vidosic's exit less than two weeks before the season's start has thrown expectations into the air. Brighton's squad was fashioned in his image, and while new head coach Arturo Ruiz impressed during his time at Real Sociedad, getting to grips with a brand new team so close to the season's beginning screams teething problems.

Charlton, Birmingham, and Crystal Palace have been promoted, with Leicester the only relegated side. Consequently, the WSL has expanded from 12 to 14 teams.

From now on, the champions of the second-tier WSL2 will win automatic promotion and the bottom WSL team will be automatically relegated. The WSL2 runners-up and 13th-placed WSL team will have a play-off to decide the final top-tier spot.

"It's a huge positive," Zelem said. "Before, it was really difficult for players to filter in, find a team, or get as many minutes as they would like. But the more teams in the league, the better, especially now that the quality is increasing. And you can see the teams coming up are putting in money and signing some great players. So that just adds to the competitiveness."

With each team playing 26 rather than 22 league fixtures, the hope is that one rogue result or dropped point will no longer have a disproportionate impact on a team's season. "It's a good thing because it means the margins aren't so small all the time," Zelem said. "Before it was such a short season and it felt a little bit dragged out, but now it'll be more flowing and less breaks hopefully."

"It gets a lot more eyes on it because there are different things going on throughout the season," Crystal Palace playmaker Annabel Blanchard said. "There's extra spice, with the play-offs and everything."

"It's also really good for the fans that it's not just (about) finishing top two or three."

The knock-on effect, though, is an increased load for those players who already juggle club and international fixtures in a tightly packed calendar.

"It's hard because the expansion is good, but on the flip side, there are players that are playing every single minute for club and country," Zelem, who is not a regular international for England, said. "It's difficult to get the balance — but that's when it is on the clubs and countries to make sure players get rest. Teams, especially the top teams, have huge squads that they need to use to keep players fresh."

Charlotte Harpur: Manchester City's squad is too thin to compete for the WSL title and the Champions League.

Megan Feringa: Tottenham Hotspur will, finally, beat one of the top three.

Cerys Jones: Arsenal will go further in the Champions League than City or Chelsea, but finish below both in the WSL.

Katie Whyatt: A team outside of the big four, most likely London City or Brighton, will make a final and become one of the historically weaker WSL sides to deliver a big 'cupset'.

articles.title: Earps, Putellas and how London City can afford their high-profile transfers
articles.summary: The names just kept coming, one after the other: Alexia Putellas, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner; Mary Earps, named the best women’s goalkeeper by FIFA in 202...
articles.body:
The names just kept coming, one after the other: Alexia Putellas, a two-time Ballon d'Or winner; Mary Earps, named the best women's goalkeeper by FIFA in 2022 and 2023; Mapi Leon, a four-time Champions League winner; and Kadidiatou Diani, who has earned more than 100 caps for France.

But how are the London City Lionesses, owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, complying with the Women's Super League's financial rules to pay these big-name players?

Kang, a Korean-American businesswoman, bought the club in 2023 , helping them win promotion to the WSL in 2025. Finishing sixth in their debut top-flight season was respectable, but this summer, they have gone big. London City have splashed out on star players — albeit mostly on free transfers — for two reasons: they want to qualify for the Champions League and increase their revenue as soon as possible.

Earnings have to rise so they can afford to pay this set of players. London City are banking on marquee names attracting larger sponsorship deals and a new fanbase that will increase revenue down the line. On Thursday they announced a first-of-its-kind multi-year front-of-shirt partnership with Nike. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Kang, however, said the value exceeds some Premier League men's teams' shirt deals and the $4million (£2.9 m) annual value of the NWSL's Atlanta expansion franchise's recent front-of-shirt agreement, believed to be the wealthiest jersey sponsorship in women's sports.

Invest before revenue is a common strategy in women's football and reflects its 'start-up' nature . In a league where attendances have stalled , London City have taken it upon themselves, for better or worse, to inject some dynamism into the WSL.

"That piece of the puzzle (revenue) is missing," Christina Philippou, associate professor in sport finance at the University of Portsmouth, tells The Athletic . "But Kang is too smart for this to be: 'Let's go wild and spend for fun'." As Kang has proven in the past , if she wants to make something happen, she will.

The WSL introduced financial rules a year ago but crucially, any breach of the salary cost could not be enforced until this upcoming season.

The WSL's permitted squad salary requirement (PSS) limits clubs to spending a proportion of revenue on players, but allows for increased spending when owners provide equity funding.

PSS limits spending on player salaries to 80 per cent of a club's annual revenues, plus an allowance for 'relevant cash funding', capped at 25 per cent of those annual revenues or £4million ($5.4m), whichever is higher.

"That allows for some owner investment to push the team forward but not go completely wild," says Philippou.

Relevant cash funding from owners doesn't have to be equity, with 'soft loans' — interest-free borrowings that are at the back of the queue when it comes to the team's liabilities — also included. For most clubs, such funding will max out at £4m. At last check (accounts for the 2024-25 financial year), only Chelsea and Arsenal recorded revenues beyond £16m, suggesting only they could inject more than £4m.

Determining a WSL team's relevant revenues will require more nuance than has previously been evident. PSS dictates clubs can't count money sent from fellow group undertakings (ie, men's teams) as revenue, and any revenue from sponsorship deals spanning both forms must be 'reasonably allocated'. That will require a clear definition of splits to be distributed between the men's and women's teams going forward.

Whatever the topline figure ends up being, clubs will only be able to spend 80 per cent of it on their 'total salary cost' — a slightly misleading tagline, as it only refers to players' wages. The WSL has laid out a list of what comprises these player salary costs, including player agent payments and image rights.

Notable exceptions include pension contributions, payments towards player education, parental leave or childcare, helping ensure that clubs don't cut back under the guise of compliance with the rules.

How much have London City spent and what are the risks?

Well, we won't know until the financial accounts are released in approximately 18 months. But according to multiple sources — speaking anonymously to protect relationships, like some others in this piece — there is no player at London City earning a baseline salary of more than £1million.

London City have been criticised for inflating wages at the top end of the market, but one source points to Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw's salary — Manchester City's star striker signed a new four-year contract in June that, as The Athletic reported, is worth an annual £1.6m , excluding performance-related bonuses. There is an argument, however, that London City's activity has driven wages at the middle-to-lower levels of the table, where clubs are fighting to build their fanbases and compete.

Over the coming years, London City plan to shift their sights to younger, more affordable players, keep wages down, and hope the allure of their squad, facilities, and the prospect of competing in Europe will attract the next generation of talent. They do not want to become the go-to team for out-of-contract 32-year-olds.

During their promotion 2024-25 season from the Championship (now WSL 2), their total expenditure (£11.5m) was the fourth-highest in English women's football, only behind Arsenal (£21.6m), Chelsea (£20.2m) and Manchester City (£14.0m). Their revenue was only £902,000, in contrast to Chelsea (£21.3m), Arsenal (£21.5m), Manchester United (£10.7m) and City (£10.6m). Generating revenue is vital now that London City have higher-earning players on their books.

The independent club has, according to a source with knowledge of the matter, developed a five-year business plan to make the project sustainable and profitable. Any club can spend now but their revenue generated at the end of the season, when they have to declare their figures, is an estimate. London City's fanbase, according to the source, has already significantly increased and sponsors are offering more because of the names attached to the club. The WSL also negotiated an improved five-year TV deal , starting from the 2025-26 season, which will increase revenue.

The risk is overestimating the impact of such transfers, especially in the case of their biggest star, Putellas. What if sponsorship deals do not come off? What if she gets injured or wants to move? What if the new fans at their ground in Bromley, south London, with a capacity of just 5,160, are not engaged as the club predicted? There are a lot of what-ifs, but London City are hedging their bets.

What are the punishments if a club breaches the PSS?

Let's be clear: there is no sense that London City have done anything wrong yet.

Perhaps learning from the past ambiguity of sanctions in the Premier League , the WSL has been prescriptive when detailing what might befall London City, or anyone, if they breach PSS.

The regulations section breaches are split into four types: minor procedural, major procedural, salary floor threshold and salary cost threshold.

The former two range in seriousness from late filings to 'attempts to circumvent' the rules in bad faith by, for example, "falsifying exclusions to redirect funds to a player and therefore reduce their salary cap value". Minor procedural breaches carry low penalties but major ones can lead to point deductions.

A salary floor threshold breach occurs when clubs are found to have paid players less than the bare minimum required by WSL rules. Those salary floors are flexed by age and tier: in the top flight, minimum salaries range from £26,900 for players aged 18-20 to £42,500 for over-23s; in WSL2, the range is £17,500 to £26,900. A breach here sees clubs allowed time to rectify the issue. If they don't, point deductions are possible.

Salary cost threshold breaches — which, from the outside, look like London City's most obvious concern — are split into their own minor and major categories.

A minor breach is when a club exceeds its threshold by up to 20 per cent and incurs a fine. They taper upwards in line with the size of the breach and can total up to 40 per cent of the club's excess spending. For example, if the maximum amount a club can spend, according to revenue generated, is £10m but they spend 20 per cent more (£12m) they will be fined 40 per cent of the £2m excess (which is £800,000).

Anything beyond a 20 per cent excess comprises a major breach and would incur a more severe fine (50 per cent of the excess) and a points deduction. If a top-flight club exceeds its salary cap by 20 per cent but by less than £100,000, they will be docked one point. Anything that is both 20 per cent and £900,000 over a club's threshold will see them docked at least 10 points. So if a club's threshold is £10m, they exceed it by 30 per cent, rising to £13m, they will be fined £1.5m and docked at least 10 points.

If clubs have not met their revenue target at the end of the season, some may embark on creative ways, such as club tours, to close the revenue gap.

Some teams in men's football could calculate that taking the financial hit and points deduction would leave them better off if they qualify for European competitions — the source, who has been briefed on the situation, stresses that is not London City's intention.

But it is still a possibility for any club.

On the one hand, bringing high-profile players into the WSL attracts more eyeballs, driving the league's growth. On the other hand, you can understand why some teams, especially mid-table clubs, may be irked. Aggressive spending widens the competitive gap between teams and creates pressure for others to invest in order to compete, potentially beyond a club's means. The financial regulations are in place to prevent clubs from doing that.

"The better your accountants and lawyers, the more wiggle room you can get," says Philippou. New regulations have lots of loopholes in them and clubs test the limits. As the league progresses, the rules get stronger and more loopholes are closed.

What is beneficial for the women's game is, when the financial accounts are published, a more transparent understanding of wage to revenue ratio. For now, London City are prepared to speculate to accumulate.

articles.title: Illinois takes down UAB in the season opener
articles.summary: Illinois moves to 1-0 on the young season.
articles.body:
Champaign, Ill — Four seconds remaining in the first half, and 54 yards away from the UAB goal line. That was the position Katin Houser was in, up only one point, on the Blazers – however, magic was about to happen.

Houser, with all the time in the world, stepped up in the pocket and fired a missile that was tipped into the hands of Ty Robinson for a touchdown, as the clock read triple zeros.

The play put Illinois (1-0) up eight heading into the half and ultimately led to their victory over the visiting UAB Blazers (0-1) by a score of 42-23.

It wasn't all sunshine and rainbows for Illinois, though. UAB gave the Illini a serious run for their money – literally. The Blazers' run game was on point in Thursday's contest, with Braylon McReynolds and Roderic Robinson II combining for 114 of the team's 194 rushing yards.

UAB also dominated the time of possession, controlling the ball for 41:03 compared to the Illini's 18:57.

To be fair, the time differential was mainly due to the Orange and Blue's success on breakaway plays.

The first one came directly after the conclusion of UAB's first drive.

Mac Resetich stood within the Illini's 10-yard line awaiting the Blazers' punt. The senior DB had just played the whole first series on defense – however, you wouldn't have been able to tell on the return. Mac took the punt 65 yards, which set up an Illini touchdown two plays later.

The touchdown would come via a Katin Houser pass to Collin Dixon, the first of two touchdowns the pair would have together.

Houser, in only his second play as an Illini, pump-faked to Brayden Trimble like it was a screen, with both Blazer DB's biting hard on it. Thus, allowing Dixon to prance into the end zone unguarded.

If we're talking big plays, though, I'd have to mention Ca'lil Valentine.

The junior running back followed up a 17-yard run with a 51-yard house call that showcased his full speed.

Valentine is up a full 20 pounds from when he arrived on campus in 2024, yet he has the same twitchiness that made him such an exciting prospect. I'd expect him to get more and more carries as the season progresses.

The game will undoubtedly be a relief for some aspects of Illinois' team. For one, Katin Houser looked eerily similar to Luke Altmyer, and the Illini DB's balled out, only allowing 219 passing yards.

However, the defense was on the field for a very long time, and if it wasn't for some undisciplined UAB penalties, today could have been a lot more costly.

However, for the first game of the Bobby Hauck and the 3-3-5 era, I gotta give credit where credit is due. The Orange and Blue, time and time again, would stop the Blazers while they were deep in their own territory. UAB had to settle the whole game, and I think it showed the mental fortitude that this Illinois team has.

One of the craziest football plays I've ever seen in person.

Valentine will be a major piece of this offense.

The cherry on top — Ismael Kante takes this interception to the house.

Katin Houser (ILL) — 13/17, 182 Passing Yards, 3 Passing TDs, 1 Rushing TD

Collin Dixon (ILL) — 70 Receiving Yards, 6 Receptions, 2 TDs

Roderic Robinson II (UAB) — 73 Total Yards, 1 Receiving TD

Ryder Burton (UAB) – 18/32, 219 Yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

The Illini are 1-0, and things are looking more exciting than ever.

The Duke Blue Devils will come to Champaign next Saturday, looking to seek revenge after Illinois beat them handily last season in Durham.
